title: talons: rules that watch and act

beats.title: a wall goes black at 3am
beats.screen_note: `/talons` on site-A, the seeded list of seven talons. Slow scroll top to bottom: "doors open — lobby wall is live", "gpu pinned on the render node", "nightly restart — media servers", "projector dropped offline", "touchdesigner crash recovery", "update guard — sundays", "weekly health report".

direction.SCREEN: `/talons` on site-A, the seeded list of seven talons. Slow scroll top to bottom: "doors open — lobby wall is live", "gpu pinned on the render node", "nightly restart — media servers", "projector dropped offline", "touchdesigner crash recovery", "update guard — sundays", "weekly health report".
direction.NOTE: capture precondition — any beat that fires a hoot action against a real machine needs the agent's one-time hoot CLI fetch already warm (`%ProgramData%\Owlette\cache\claude-cli\claude.exe`, ~240 MB, downloaded on first use). Run one hoot action on the capture machine the day before, or the take stalls on the download.

beats.title: trigger, condition, outputs
beats.screen_note: click "create talon" → the "new talon" dialog. Hold on the three cards left to right with the connector wires between them: TRIGGER | CONDITION | OUTPUTS. Open the trigger dropdown so all three options show — "on a schedule", "when a metric crosses", "when an event happens" — then close it.

direction.SCREEN: click "create talon" → the "new talon" dialog. Hold on the three cards left to right with the connector wires between them: TRIGGER | CONDITION | OUTPUTS. Open the trigger dropdown so all three options show — "on a schedule", "when a metric crosses", "when an event happens" — then close it.

beats.title: build one live
beats.screen_note: trigger → "when an event happens", tick `process_crash` in the event list. Condition stays on "always run outputs", machines stays "all machines". Outputs row 1: type "command" → "restart process" → pick TouchDesigner. "add output" → row 2 type "email". Type the name "touchdesigner crash recovery" → "create talon" → the row appears in the list.

direction.SCREEN: trigger → "when an event happens", tick `process_crash` in the event list. Condition stays on "always run outputs", machines stays "all machines". Outputs row 1: type "command" → "restart process" → pick TouchDesigner. "add output" → row 2 type "email". Type the name "touchdesigner crash recovery" → "create talon" → the row appears in the list.
direction.NOTE: the `command` output type only appears in the picker for a site admin — capture signed in as the admin fixture user.

beats.title: start from a preset
beats.screen_note: reopen "create talon"; open the "start from a template…" picker in the dialog header. Show the group labels — "ready to use" / "needs a detail" — then choose "morning wall check" and let every field populate.

direction.SCREEN: reopen "create talon"; open the "start from a template…" picker in the dialog header. Show the group labels — "ready to use" / "needs a detail" — then choose "morning wall check" and let every field populate.
direction.NOTE: the grouping is per-viewer: with an ai key saved in settings → hoot all six built-ins sit under "ready to use"; with no key the five ai-backed ones drop to "needs a detail" with the hint "needs an ai api key — add one in settings → hoot". Capture whichever state you want on screen by seeding (or clearing) the fixture user's llm key first.

beats.title: the visual check
beats.screen_note: in the condition card, switch to "visual check". Show the "what should be on screen" box with the wall expectation text, the monitor field ("0 = all monitors, 1 = primary"), and the hint beneath: "hoot grabs a fresh screenshot and checks it against this… the outputs fire when the check FAILS." Cut to a run row on the list showing `verdict: fail — <reason>`.

direction.SCREEN: in the condition card, switch to "visual check". Show the "what should be on screen" box with the wall expectation text, the monitor field ("0 = all monitors, 1 = primary"), and the hint beneath: "hoot grabs a fresh screenshot and checks it against this… the outputs fire when the check FAILS." Cut to a run row on the list showing `verdict: fail — <reason>`.

beats.title: let hoot act
beats.screen_note: change an output's type to "hoot"; show the directive box, then the "let hoot act" switch and the copy under it. Toggle it on, hold two beats, toggle it back off.

direction.SCREEN: change an output's type to "hoot"; show the directive box, then the "let hoot act" switch and the copy under it. Toggle it on, hold two beats, toggle it back off.

beats.title: run history, cooldown, auto-disable
beats.screen_note: expand a talon row's chevron → the "recent runs" block. Show the run rows: status glyph, trigger summary + machine, the `2/2 sent` count, duration, "12m ago", and a "view hoot chat" link on the row that started one. Hover the "run now" (↺) and pause buttons in the row's action cluster.

direction.SCREEN: expand a talon row's chevron → the "recent runs" block. Show the run rows: status glyph, trigger summary + machine, the `2/2 sent` count, duration, "12m ago", and a "view hoot chat" link on the row that started one. Hover the "run now" (↺) and pause buttons in the row's action cluster.
direction.NOTE: `automate-talons-list` seeds talon docs only, NOT `sites/{siteId}/talon_runs` — expanding a row in that scenario shows the "no runs yet" empty state. Either extend the fixture with run docs before recording, or capture this beat against a live dev site with real history.

beats.title: the one to turn on first
beats.screen_note: open "create talon" → template picker → "update guard"; the fields fill in with the sunday 07:00 schedule and a single hoot output, and the "let hoot act" switch is OFF. Toggle it on, then cut back to the "update guard — sundays" row in the list and pull out to the whole list of seven.

direction.SCREEN: open "create talon" → template picker → "update guard"; the fields fill in with the sunday 07:00 schedule and a single hoot output, and the "let hoot act" switch is OFF. Toggle it on, then cut back to the "update guard — sundays" row in the list and pull out to the whole list of seven.
direction.NOTE: show the switch state from the PRESET (off), not from the seeded `talon-update-guard` fixture row — that fixture instance is written with `allowActions: true` and would contradict the line about it arriving without permission to act.
